articles.title: Trump lashes out at Fed after Warsh-backed rate hike, demands rates of 1% or less
articles.description: Trump has renewed pressure on the Federal Reserve, demanding rates of 1% or lower shortly after the central bank raised its benchmark rate to 3.75%-4% to tackle persistent inflation. The move has put Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, Trump’s own appointee, in the spotlight, as Warsh defended the hike and warned that inflation remains too high. The clash also highlights tensions over the Fed’s independence, with Trump linking interest rates to US trade deficits and continuing his broader criticism of officials he has appointed.

articles.title: North Korea to expand nuclear arsenal as 'US-led buildup justifies it'

This declaration follows intense trilateral military exercises and recent missile tests, with Pyongyang firmly rejecting any requests for denuclearization, emphasizing its need for self-defense.

articles.title: How 3 Italians took flight from India sans immigration check: hub-spoke model, govt action explained
articles.description: How could three Italians take flights from two Indian airports and reach their international destination without clearing mandatory immigration? This question is gripping India's aviation sector after a show-cause notice was issued to Air India over the Italian nationals flying from Amritsar to Delhi on an Air India flight in the early hours of September 4. They were then scheduled to travel onward from Delhi to Munich on Lufthansa flight LH-763. But there was a problem. The Ministry says the three passengers left India on the Lufthansa flight without undergoing mandatory departure immigration clearance. Here's what happened, how the government reacted, and what happens next. Watch the full video for more.

articles.title: He trusted Canara Bank for 31 Years, then was sold a life insurance plan that pays at age 93; IRDAI orders Rs 4 lakh refund and ₹1 crore fine for mis-selling
articles.description: IRDAI has imposed a ₹1 crore penalty on Canara HSBC Life Insurance Company over the sale of a deferred annuity policy to an 88-year-old customer who had been banking with Canara Bank for 31 years. The policy required ₹2 lakh annual premiums for four years and named his 57-year-old daughter as the annuitant. IRDAI found several lapses in the sale and verification process. The insurer refunded ₹4.09 lakh to the customer.
